newsitem.title: UK: Crude tanker rates healthy for Mideast/west VLCCs.
newsitem.headline: Crude tanker rates healthy for Mideast/west VLCCs.

text.p: Crude oil tanker chartering rates were steady to slightly firmer on Tuesday for Mideast/US routes amid a steady stream of fixtures, brokers said.
"The underlying tone is slightly firmer," one said.

Brokers noted KPC's fixtures of the 390,000 tonne Marine Pacific from the Mideast to the US Gulf at W45, using 1997 worldscale rates. This would put this year's rates for ULCCs at around W49, the broker said.
Officials at the Iraqi oil loading terminal of Mina al-Bakr said the 265,000 tonne tanker Leonidas was currently loading and was due to sail on Wednesday.
A number of brokers said they felt the crude had been fixed to move to the Red Sea and not to the U.S. Gulf, as earlier reported.
Rates for the Leonidas and the Star Africa, also due to load at al-Bakr, were low because they were old ships, brokers said.

Old ships were currently being fixed from that port because they had been easier to obtain at short notice than the newer ships. But there was no reason why newer vessels should not be fixed from that port in the near future, they added.
Rates for eastwards journeys for VLCCs from the Mideast were little changed, with 250,000 tonners to Japan paying W62.5.

West African rates for 130,000 tonne suezmaxes were steady for westwards voyages and fixtures were seen at around W82.5-W85. One two-million barrel vessel, the World Champion, was also seen moving transatlantic at W62.5.
Brokers said fuel oil rates in northwest Europe were holding up fairly well for 25,000 tonne ships at around W190.
"I think we will continue to see W190 for the time being," one broker said. But there were few fresh enquiries in the Mediterranean and dealers saw some room for rates to slip.
